comments.body:
Implementation in worktree ../doctor-lock-health (branch doctor-lock-health from origin/main 70679d3c21).

New module src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py (386 LOC) + wiring in doctor.py (332 LOC, both under the 800 cap). Semantics shipped:
- Four legs reported every run: tickets-write-fcntl, tickets-write-mkdir, hlc, enrich-drain.
- State vocabulary held/free/absent/unknown. fcntl legs probed with the same zero-deadline flock(LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB) + errno discrimination write_lock_is_busy uses, opened WITHOUT O_CREAT so a diagnostic never creates a lock file.
- mkdir leg decodes the v2 stamp via lock_owner._parse_v2_stamp (host/ns/pid/start), liveness via _describe_stamped_pid (same-host only; 'unprobeable (foreign host)' / '(other pid namespace)' elsewhere), age via _mkdir_lock_age_s.
- Staleness is ONLY lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale(lock_dir, fcntl_held=False). No second heuristic anywhere in the module; the pid-recycle qualification and the wall-clock ceiling are inherited.
- fcntl legs get staleness 'not-applicable' (kernel releases on holder death); the O_EXCL drain lock gets 'not-assessable' (no ownership stamp — reported with its age, never guessed at).
- Exit code: only a 'stale' leg becomes a lock_findings entry and forces exit 1. A held lock with a live holder is INFO and keeps exit 0. Lock results live in their own list so doctor --repair's loop can never reach a lock.
- JSON envelope gains 'locks' and 'lock_findings'; schema and the pinned help text (regenerated into docs/cli-reference.md) updated.

Smoke test against the live tracker found a REAL leaked .rebar/enrich-drain.lock held ~26 days on this host — filed separately and linked discovered_from.

Cross-link: this is the observability half of bug sunlit-cynical-ray (84af-8d4f-bc1c-41b9), which removes the long lock hold itself; linked relates_to.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
On 2026-08-12 a session was blocked on the tickets write lock for 15+ minutes: a
`transition ... closed` (pid 61327) held both legs of the store write lock
(`.ticket-write.lock` and `.ticket-write.lock.d`) for the whole LLM completion
verification. rebar had NO diagnostic surface for this — the operator had to `ls` the
lock dir and `cat` the owner stamp by hand to learn who held it and whether that
process was still alive. `rebar doctor` today only audits blocking links, so an
operator facing a wedged store has nothing to run.

The lock-hold defect itself is bug `sunlit-cynical-ray` (84af-8d4f-bc1c-41b9), fixed in
parallel. This ticket is the OBSERVABILITY half and does not change locking behaviour:
even after 84af lands, a held or orphaned lock still needs to be inspectable.

## Approach
Add a read-only lock-health section to `rebar doctor`. All the primitives already exist
and are REUSED, not re-derived:

- `rebar._store.lock.write_lock_is_busy` — the existing zero-deadline both-legs probe.
  Its immediate-probe technique (fcntl `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB`, `mkdir`, give straight back)
  is what the per-leg probes use, so held/free is answered without waiting.
- `rebar._store.lock_owner._parse_v2_stamp` / `_describe_stamped_pid` /
  `_mkdir_lock_age_s` — the v2 owner stamp (host/ns/pid/start), the same-host-only
  liveness verdict (`live` / `not-running` / `unprobeable (...)`), and the hold age.
- `rebar._store.lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale(lock_dir, fcntl_held=False)` — the SOLE
  staleness authority. No second heuristic is written; the pid-recycle qualification and
  the wall-clock ceiling from the existing decision table are inherited as-is.
  `fcntl_held=False` because doctor holds nothing.

Legs reported: the tracker's fcntl leg `.ticket-write.lock`, the tracker's mkdir leg
`.ticket-write.lock.d`, `.rebar/hlc.lock` (fcntl, probed the same non-blocking way), and
`.rebar/enrich-drain.lock` (an `O_EXCL` existence lock, so held == file exists). The
drain lock carries no owner stamp; its staleness is reported as `not-assessable` rather
than guessed at, because inventing a heuristic for it is exactly what this plan forbids.

Doctor is READ-ONLY here: nothing is reclaimed or deleted, and `--repair` does not touch
locks (its repair loop iterates only the link findings list, which lock results never
join). A held lock with a live holder is INFO. A lock the shared staleness function
calls stale is a FINDING and joins doctor's existing exit-code rule (exit 1 when
anything is outstanding, 0 otherwise).

Because `_commands/doctor.py` is a link-audit module, the lock checks land in a new
sibling module `_commands/doctor_locks.py` along the existing command-module seam (the
same split `fsck.py`/`fsck_repair.py` uses); `doctor.py` calls one entry point and
renders the result.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor_locks.py` (new) — leg probes, stamp decode, report + finding
  construction, text rendering.
- `src/rebar/_commands/doctor.py` — call the scan, add `locks` / `lock_findings` to the
  JSON envelope and the text output, fold lock findings into the exit code.
- `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` — describe the two new keys.
- `docs/cli-reference.md` — document the lock section under `rebar doctor`.
- `tests/scripts/graph/test_doctor.py` (or a new sibling test module) — the tests below.

## Testing
- Happy path: a free store reports every leg `free`, no lock findings, exit unchanged (0).
- Held-and-healthy: holding the real write lock via `lock.write_lock`, doctor reports the
  mkdir leg held, names host/pid from the stamp, reports a non-negative hold age and a
  live pid state, and produces NO finding (INFO only) — so exit stays 0.
- Stale/dead holder: a mkdir lock dir stamped with a v2 stamp for a dead pid on this host
  produces a `stale-lock` finding and exit 1.
- Unreadable/absent stamp: a lock dir with no owner file reports `unknown (no ownership
  stamp)` and does not crash; a `.rebar` dir that does not exist reports the two `.rebar`
  legs as absent rather than raising.
- Read-only guarantee: after a doctor run over a held lock, the lock dir, its owner file
  and the drain lock file all still exist byte-identical (doctor never reclaims).
- JSON contract: `--output json` validates against the updated doctor schema.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `rebar doctor` reports, for each of the four legs, held/free (or absent), and for
      the mkdir leg the v2 stamp fields host/ns/pid/start, holder liveness, and hold age —
      verified by the held-and-healthy test asserting those fields in `--output json`.
- [ ] Holder liveness is same-host only: a stamp from another host identity or another pid
      namespace reports an `unprobeable (...)` verdict, never a pid guess — verified by a
      test stamping a foreign host identity.
- [ ] Staleness comes only from `lock_owner._mkdir_lock_is_stale`; a grep of the new module
      shows no second staleness heuristic (no independent age threshold, no independent pid
      probe used to decide stale).
- [ ] A dead-holder lock yields a finding and `rebar doctor` exits 1; a live-holder lock
      yields no finding and exits 0 — verified by the two tests above.
- [ ] Doctor never mutates lock state: the read-only test shows lock dir, owner file and
      drain lock file unchanged after a run, and `--repair` performs no lock action.
- [ ] `--output json` matches `src/rebar/schemas/doctor.schema.json` and
      `docs/cli-reference.md` documents the lock section — verified by the schema test and
      the docs diff.
- [ ] All `src/rebar` files stay under the 800-LOC module cap (module-size gate green).
